dangerous_cpts.main_problem: This CPT has the strongest failure-specific signal: the same parameter (column 7 -> Compromised) appears in 5 failure scenarios and 0 success scenarios, and it is part of a repeated failure activation pattern together with Program_Anomaly. Structurally, this node is the key integrator from program/log anomalies and response/dispatch deviations into the final diagnosis. In the domain, execution integrity should be strongly tied to true application compromise, but column 7 maps a specific upstream configuration to Compromised with high confidence (0.8). Because this parameter sits between intermediate evidence and Root_Causes, repeated wrong predictions are plausibly amplified here rather than being fully explained by downstream classification alone.

suspicious_parameters.justification: This parameter is activated only in failures among the observed scenarios and repeatedly co-occurs with Program_Anomaly column 1 in the common failure pattern. The CPT currently makes Compromised the argmax with strong confidence for the parent configuration (Program_Anomaly=No, Deviation_in_Response=No, Deviation_in_Dispatch=Yes). Domain-wise, dispatch-side expected deviations alone should not necessarily imply compromised execution when program anomaly evidence is absent, so the current probability may be too aggressive.

dangerous_cpts.main_problem: This CPT shows a repeated failure-associated parameter with limited success overlap: column 1 -> No is activated in 5 failure scenarios versus 2 success scenarios. It also participates directly in the most common failure activation pattern with Execution_Integrity. Semantically, GPTN_3 captures inconsistent execution logs, which are important evidence for application anomalies. If this CPT too readily outputs Program_Anomaly=No when GPTN_3 is Not_Found, it can suppress compromise evidence and distort downstream execution-integrity reasoning across multiple failures.

suspicious_parameters.justification: For GPTN_3=Not_Found, the CPT strongly favors No (0.9). In this domain, absence of inconsistent log evidence does not reliably prove absence of program anomaly because logs may be imperfect or incomplete. The repeated failure pattern suggests this strong negative mapping may be causing under-detection of program anomalies, which then feeds into incorrect Execution_Integrity and final root-cause predictions.

overall_summary: Execution_Integrity and Program_Anomaly are the only CPTs with strong enough independent evidence for refinement search. Both lie on the same repeated failure path, but each has its own plausible modeling issue: Program_Anomaly may overinterpret missing log inconsistency as evidence of normality, and Execution_Integrity may overinterpret dispatch-only deviation evidence as compromise even when program anomaly and response deviation are absent. Network_Manipulation and Root_Causes were not included because their evidence is weaker and more plausibly explained by upstream reasoning errors rather than independent CPT flaws.
